Rashi on Shabbat 133a:10:1.hebrew: שאין תלמוד לומר עד בקר - תניינא, "והנותר ממנו עד בקר", דמצי למכתב "והנותר באש תשרפו". אלא אשריפה קאי, והכי קאמר: "והנותר ממנו" בזמן שאסרתי לך, דהיינו בקר ראשון, כשיבא בקר שני שהוא חולו של מועד — "תשרפו", אבל בי"ט לא. אלמא, מידי דחול לא עבדינן בי"ט. ופסח, קרבן י"ד בניסן הוא שהוא חול; ומילה שלא בזמנה נמי מידי דחול הוא, דבשבת זו לא היה זמנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:10:1.english: As [the Torah] did not need to state "until morning" - [This refers to] the second [mention]: "and that which remains of it until morning," for [Scripture] could have written, "and that which remains, you shall burn with fire." Rather, it refers to the burning, and this is what [the verse] is saying: "And that which remains of it" at the time that I prohibited [it] to you — which is the first morning — when the second morning arrives, which is Chol HaMoed, "you shall burn [it]," but on Yom Tov, no. Thus, we see that we do not perform a weekday matter on Yom Tov. And the Pesach [offering] is a sacrifice of the 14th of Nisan, which is a weekday; and circumcision not in its [proper] time is also a weekday matter, for on this Shabbat it was not its [proper] time.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:11:1.hebrew: ולא עולת חול בי"ט - אברי תמיד של עי"ט אין קרבין בי"ט, ומילה שלא בזמנה נמי כעולת חול בי"ט דמי:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:11:1.english: And not the burnt-offering of a weekday on a Festival - The limbs of the daily burnt-offering of the eve of a Festival are not offered on the Festival, and circumcision not in its [proper] time is also like a burnt-offering of a weekday on a Festival.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:12:1.hebrew: דאתיא בק"ו - שתדחה: ומה צרעת שדוחה עבודה, מילה שלא בזמנה דוחה אותה כדאמרינן לעיל; שבת שנדחית מפני עבודה, אינו דין שמילה שלא בזמנה דוחה אותה? להכי איצטריך לבדו:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:12:1.english: Which is derived through an a fortiori inference - that it would override [Shabbat]: if tzara'at, which overrides the Temple service, is overridden by circumcision not at its [appointed] time, as we said above; [then] Shabbat, which is overridden by the Temple service, is it not logical that circumcision not at its [appointed] time should override it? Therefore, "alone" is needed.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:13:1.hebrew: ואין עשה - דמילה דוחה לא תעשה ועשה, אבל בזמנה איתרבי מביום אפילו בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:13:1.english: And a positive commandment does not - [that] of circumcision override a negative commandment and a positive commandment; however, in its [proper] time, it is derived from [the word] "on the day" [that it overrides] even Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:15:1.hebrew: גבי פסח - כל מלאכה שאפשר לה לעשות מע"ש, כגון הבאתו מחוץ לתחום וחתיכת יבלתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:15:1.english: Pertaining to the Paschal lamb - Any [prohibited] labor that can be performed on Shabbat eve, such as bringing it from outside the [Shabbat] boundary and cutting off its wart.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:16:1.hebrew: וצריכא - למימר בתרוייהו הלכה כר"ע, דמכשירין לא דחו:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:16:1.english: And [it] was necessary - to state in both of them [that] the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, that facilitators do not override [Shabbat].

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:16:2.hebrew: מילה בזמנה ליכא כרת - דקטן לאו בר עונשין הוא, ואבוה לא מיחייב עליה כרת:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:16:2.english: Circumcision in its [proper] time, there is no karet - For a minor is not subject to punishment, and his father is not liable to karet for it.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:18:2.english: And [they] uncover - the skin that covers the head of the organ.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:18:3.hebrew: ומוצצין - את הדם, ואף על גב דהיא עשיית חבורה, שאין הדם ניתק מחיבורו אלא על ידי המציצה:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:18:3.english: And [one] sucks - the blood. And even though it is [considered] making a wound, since the blood is not detached from its attachment except through the sucking, [it is nevertheless permitted].

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:19:1.english: He chews [it] with his teeth - As much as it is possible to deviate [from the usual manner], we deviate [from it].

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:19:2.hebrew: לא טרף יין ושמן - כך היו רגילין, והיא רפואה, שמערבין וטורפין בקערה יין ושמן יחד, כדרך שטורפין ביצים בקערה:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:19:2.english: [If] he did not beat wine and oil - This was their custom, and it is a remedy, that they mix and beat wine and oil together in a bowl, just as one beats eggs in a bowl.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:1:1.hebrew: תנאי היא - דאיכא דנפקא ליה מילה בזמנה מק"ו כרבא, וכי אתא קרא לשלא בזמנה. ואיכא דלא נפקא ליה בק"ו, ואיצטריך למילה בזמנה כרב ספרא, ושלא בזמנה אתיא מביניא:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:1:1.english: It is [a dispute of] tanna’im - For there is [one tanna] who derives circumcision at its proper time from an a fortiori inference, like Rava, and when the verse comes, [it comes] for [circumcision] not at its proper time. And there is [another tanna] who does not derive it through an a fortiori inference, and [the verse] is needed for circumcision at its proper time, like Rav Safra, and [circumcision] not at its proper time is derived from between [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:20:1.hebrew: חלוק - כעין כיס דחוק היו עושין, ומלבישים את ראש הגיד עד העטרה וקושרים שם, כדי שלא יחזור העור לכסות את הגיד:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:20:1.english: A tunic - They would make [something] like a tight pouch and slip [it] over the head of the member up to the corona, and tie [it] there, so that the skin would not return to cover the member.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:20:2.english: He did not prepare - He did not ready [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:20:3.hebrew: כורך על ידו - דרך מלבוש, לשנותו מדרך הוצאה בחול:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:20:3.english: He wraps [it] on his hand - In the manner of a garment, to alter it from the [ordinary] manner of carrying out on a weekday.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:3:1.hebrew: לרבי יהודה - רבי יאשיה דמצריך קרא להכי, כרבי יהודה סבירא ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:3:1.english: According to Rabbi Yehuda - Rabbi Yoshiyah, who requires a verse for this, holds like Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:3:2.hebrew: מודה ר' שמעון בפסיק כו' - הילכך, אי לא רבי קרא, לא עבדי:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:3:2.english: Rabbi Shimon concedes in [the case of] "cut off [its head]," etc. - Therefore, if the verse had not included [it], they would not do [so].

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:3:3.english: He accepted it - He set his mind to it and accepted [it] from him.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:4:1.hebrew: ה"ג לעשות עושה אתה בסיב שעל רגלו ובמוט שעל גבי כתיפו - ואינו צריך להזהר מלדחות סיב שקושר מנעלו ברגלו, ומלישא משאוי על כתיפו:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:4:1.english: This is the reading: “To do [you may not do, but] you may do with a fiber that is on his foot and with a pole that is on his shoulder” - And he does not need to be careful not to press [with] a fiber with which he ties his shoe on his foot, nor [to refrain] from carrying a load on his shoulder.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:4:2.hebrew: ואם עברה - הבהרת בכך, עברה, ואינו חושש לה. להכי כתיב ״לעשות״, שמותר לעשות מלאכתו:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:4:2.english: And if it is removed - [i.e.,] the bright white spot [is removed] thereby, it is removed, and he is not concerned about it. For this reason it is written “to do,” [teaching] that it is permitted to do his work.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:6:1.hebrew: ואביי אליבא דר' שמעון - מעיקרא, מקמי דסברה, האי בשר מאי עביד ליה:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:6:1.english: And Abaye, according to Rabbi Shimon - Initially, before he accepted it [i.e., Rava's reasoning], what does he do with this [word] "flesh"?

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:6:2.hebrew: באומר לקוץ - גדול שהוא בר עונשין, ואומר למוהל לקוץ בהרתו בכוונה ליטהר:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:6:2.english: In [a case where] he says to cut off - [This refers to] an adult who is subject to punishment, and he says to the mohel to cut off his bright white spot intentionally in order to become pure.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:7:1.hebrew: קטן - דלא ידע לכווני, מאי איכא למימר? ועל כרחיך בתרוייהו כתיב בשר, כדאמרי' לעיל; ובשר דכתיב גבי קטן ביום השמיני, ל"ל:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:7:1.english: A minor - Who does not know [how] to have intention, what is there to say? And perforce, in both of them "flesh" is written, as we said above; so why do I need [the word] "flesh" that is written regarding a minor [who is circumcised] on the eighth day?

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:7:2.hebrew: באומר אבי הבן לקוץ - דמתכוין לטהרו, והוא מוזהר דלא ליעבד בידים ובמתכוין:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:7:2.english: Where the father of the child says [his intention is] to cut off - For he intends to purify him, and he is warned not to do [so] actively and intentionally.

Rashi on Shabbat 133a:8:1.hebrew: ואי איכא אחר - שאינו חושש לטהרו, ליעבד אחר ולא ליקו אב להתם, ואע"ג דרבייה קרא, שהרי אתה יכול לקיים עשה בלא עקירת לאו לר' שמעון, דהא אחר לא מיכוין ולא עבר, ואמר ריש לקיש כו'. ורבויא למאי אתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 133a:8:1.english: And if there is another [person] - who is not concerned to purify him, let another [person] perform [the circumcision] and let the father not step up to it, even though Scripture included [it]; for you can fulfill a positive commandment without uprooting a negative commandment according to Rabbi Shimon, since another [person] does not intend [to cut off the spot] and does not transgress, and Reish Lakish said, etc. And for what [purpose] did the inclusionary derivation come?

Tosafot on Shabbat 133a:15:1.hebrew: ותנן נמי גבי פסח כה"ג אמר רב יהודה אמר רב הלכה כר"ע - והכא לא פריך "הילכתא למשיחא", משום דנפקא מינה גבי מילה. אע"ג דגבי מילה נמי פסיק הכי, מ"מ לאלומי פיסקא דמילה פסיק נמי גבי פסח אגב דפסיק גבי מילה, דתילף מינה שפסק ברור הוא לכל דבר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 133a:15:1.english: And we also learned pertaining to the Paschal lamb, in a similar vein... Rav Yehuda said [that] Rav said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Akiva - And here [the Gemara] does not ask, "[Is this] a halakha for the Messianic era?" because there is a practical consequence from it regarding circumcision. Even though regarding circumcision [it] also rules thus, nevertheless, in order to strengthen the ruling regarding circumcision, [it] also rules regarding the Paschal lamb alongside ruling regarding circumcision, so that you should learn from it that it is a clear ruling for every matter.

Tosafot on Shabbat 133a:16:1.hebrew: וצריכא דאי אשמועינן - אדרב יהוד' קאי, דפסיק כר"ע הכא והתם; דאי אדרבי עקיבא, א"כ בפ' שתי הלחם (מנחות דף צו.) דקתני נמי "כלל אמר ר"ע", הוה ליה למימר "וצריכא". וכן פירש בקונטרס:
Tosafot on Shabbat 133a:16:1.english: "And [both] were necessary, for if [it] had taught us" - [This] refers to Rav Yehudah, who ruled in accordance with Rabbi Akiva here and there [i.e., regarding both circumcision and the Paschal lamb]; for if [it referred] to Rabbi Akiva [himself], then in the chapter [entitled] Shtei HaLechem (Menachot 96a), where it also teaches, "Rabbi Akiva stated a general rule," [the Gemara] should have said, "And [it] was necessary." And so Rashi explained:

Tosafot on Shabbat 133a:18:1.hebrew: עושין כל צרכי מילה בשבת - אע"ג דלעיל נמי קתני בשילהי מפנין (שבת ד' קכח.), התם תני לה אגב גררא דמילי דתינוק, אבל הכא עיקר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 133a:18:1.english: One performs all the necessities of circumcision on Shabbat - Even though above [the Mishnah] also taught [this] at the end of [the chapter] Mefanin (Shabbat 128a), there it taught it incidentally among matters concerning an infant, whereas here is [its] primary [place].

Tosafot on Shabbat 133a:19:1.hebrew: לועס בשיניו - אף על גב דאחר מילה חולה שיש בו סכנה הוא, מ"מ כמה דאפשר לשנויי משנינן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 133a:19:1.english: He chews [it] with his teeth - Even though after circumcision he is [considered] a dangerously ill patient, nevertheless, as much as it is possible to deviate [from the normal manner], we deviate.

Tosafot on Shabbat 133a:6:1.hebrew: ואביי אליבא דר' שמעון - ולרבי יונתן לא מיבעיא ליה, דמוקי ליה בינוני; ולאביי נמי דאמר לעיל דבינוני אתי מביניא, מצי למימר דסבר ר' יונתן: מילתא דאתי בק"ו, טרח וכתב לה קרא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 133a:6:1.english: "And [according to] Abaye, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon" - And [the Gemara] does not raise this question according to Rabbi Yonatan, because he establishes it [the word "flesh"] as referring to an intermediate [child]; and even according to Abaye, who said above that an intermediate [child] is derived from the combination [of an adult and a minor], one can say that Rabbi Yonatan holds that [even for] a matter that is derived through an a fortiori inference [kal vachomer], Scripture takes the trouble to write it explicitly:

Tosafot on Shabbat 133a:6:2.hebrew: באומר לקוץ בהרתו הוא מתכוין - וא"ת: אם כן, אמאי קאמר אביי "לא נצרכא אלא לרבי יהודה"? הא לר"ש נמי איצטריך, כדאמר הכא! ויש לומר דלשון ברייתא משמע דמיירי בלא מתכוין, מדלא קתני: "בשר — אע"ג דמתכוין לקוץ בהרת, ימול":
Tosafot on Shabbat 133a:6:2.english: "[It refers to] one who says his intention is to cut off his bright white spot" - And if you ask: If so, why did Abaye say, "[The verse] is needed only according to Rabbi Yehuda"? Surely it is also needed according to Rabbi Shimon, as [Rav Amram] states here! One can answer that the wording of the baraita implies that it is dealing with [a case where he] does not intend [to cut it off], since it does not teach: "'Flesh' — even though he intends to cut off a bright white spot, he may circumcise."
